title: Industry-specific ratios for banking and insurance; basis column on all ratio rows
points: Banking ratios added: cost-to-income (operating expenses / total income) and net interest margin (net interest income / total assets, using latest-prior-or-same-date balance sheet). These join the universal ratios already computed for banks.

Insurance ratios added: loss ratio, expense ratio, combined ratio (loss + expense), underwriting margin, and investment yield — all denominated on net premium written. Tickers are identified by the presence of the net_premium canonical rather than any hardcoded list.

Income field fallback chain for net_margin and asset_turnover extended from two legs to four: revenue_net (corporates) → total_income (banks) → net_premium (insurance) → operating_revenue (holding companies such as IGIHL and FCSC). Each leg fires only when all prior legs are absent for that exact ticker-period pair.

A basis TEXT column is now present on every row in the ratios table. It records the canonical name of the denominator field used in the calculation — for example net_premium for insurance net margins or total_income for bank net margins. This is the authoritative signal for labelling a ratio correctly when shown to users.

P&L-only ratios (net_margin, gross_margin, cost_to_income, all insurance ratios) are computed across 3M / 6M / 9M / 12M / LTM periods. Ratios that join to a balance sheet item (ROE, ROA, asset_turnover, net_interest_margin) remain restricted to 12M / LTM to ensure the income period is annualised before dividing by a point-in-time balance sheet figure.
Total ratio rows: 63,457 across 20 distinct ratio names (up from 56,908 across 7 names before this change).
